waive.TypeOK: Shape check only: every behaviour change below that leaves the declared types also breaks a named property, and TLC already stops with an evaluation error when an action leaves a variable unspecified.

mutations.name: drop-client-seq-duplicate-check
mutations.why: store.append no longer looks for (client, seq) in the log before the base check (design invariant 2 removed). Checked against an engine that replays a submit whose seq the log already holds, with the current head as base (MC_rogue.cfg): the server must hold invariant 2 whatever a client sends. With engines that follow section 5 the check is redundant: see mutations-observations.json.

mutations.name: drop-client-seq-duplicate-check-dup-op
mutations.why: The same mistake seen by P1: the replayed submit is appended a second time and its ops are in the document twice.

mutations.name: drop-base-equals-head-check
mutations.why: store.append appends whatever base the submit carries (design invariant 1 removed): two clients that submit at the same time are both appended. Since the drift step the engine meets the doomed client's ack and its own change with a protocol error (engine.ts:488, 500) instead of confirming them, so the edit is never confirmed and the client reconnects until it runs out of connections: P4 fails, not P2 (before the drift step it failed on P2).

mutations.name: drop-base-equals-head-check-ack
mutations.why: The same mistake seen by the derived check: an ack arrives for a doomed in-flight (before the drift step the doomed client then resent its ops and P1 failed).

mutations.name: drop-base-equals-head-check-server
mutations.why: The same mistake, seen by the server's own invariant 1: a change lands at a version other than base + 1.

mutations.name: change-inflight-on-reconnect
mutations.why: After catch-up the engine folds pending into the in-flight and resends it with the same seq and base, without proof that the copy on the dead connection can never be appended (design invariant 5).

mutations.name: change-inflight-on-reconnect-late-copy-wins
mutations.why: The same mistake where the old copy is not fenced: it is appended, the engine confirms the folded ops, and an op shown as confirmed is in no change.

mutations.name: foreign-change-does-not-doom
mutations.why: A foreign change at confirmed + 1 moves the in-flight ops into pending but leaves the in-flight live: its stale then puts the same ops in front of pending a second time.
mutations.search: IF i.s # 0 THEN [i EXCEPT !.doomed = TRUE, !.ops = <<>>] ELSE i]

mutations.name: foreign-change-does-not-doom-base
mutations.why: The same mistake seen by the derived rule: a live in-flight is left on a base the client has moved past.
mutations.search: IF i.s # 0 THEN [i EXCEPT !.doomed = TRUE, !.ops = <<>>] ELSE i]

mutations.name: foreign-change-does-not-doom-stale
mutations.why: The same mistake seen by the observation: a stale now answers an in-flight that is not doomed.
mutations.search: IF i.s # 0 THEN [i EXCEPT !.doomed = TRUE, !.ops = <<>>] ELSE i]

mutations.name: no-resend-after-catch-up
mutations.why: After a reconnect the engine waits for the ack of a not-doomed in-flight instead of resending it; the ack died with the old connection.
mutations.search: /\ c2s' = [c2s EXCEPT ![c][conn[c]] = Append(@, Submit(i.s, i.b, r.ops))]

mutations.name: no-resend-after-catch-up-liveness
mutations.why: The same mistake seen by the liveness form of P4.
mutations.search: /\ c2s' = [c2s EXCEPT ![c][conn[c]] = Append(@, Submit(i.s, i.b, r.ops))]

mutations.name: remove-fairness
mutations.why: Nothing forces a client to keep handling frames or the server to read a live connection: P4 must fail by stuttering.

mutations.name: resume-skips-a-version
mutations.why: The reconnect hello resumes from confirmed + 1 instead of confirmed, so catch-up starts one version too late.

mutations.name: stale-head-ahead-of-sent-changes
mutations.why: The server answers stale with a head one past the changes it has sent on that socket (it reads head after a concurrent append).

mutations.name: drop-attempt-fence
mutations.why: decideHello welcomes a resume hello whatever its attempt (the fix of F1 removed): a late hello of a given-up connection supersedes the live one and the client fails with edits unsent.

mutations.name: attempt-not-recorded
mutations.why: welcome does not record the attempt it welcomed (state.clients keeps the old one), so the fence compares with a stale number and lets a late hello through.
mutations.search: welcomed' = [welcomed EXCEPT ![c] = IF accept THEN f.h ELSE @]

mutations.name: link-passes-superseded-of-given-up-socket
mutations.why: Without the connectId fence of the page link, the superseded the server sends on a given-up socket reaches the engine on its current connection and fails it.
mutations.search: ELSE IF conn[c] \in closed THEN Append(@, Superseded)
mutations.replace: ELSE IF closed # {} \/ ~accept THEN Append(@, Superseded)

mutations.name: broadcast-to-socket-before-welcome
mutations.why: onSubmit sends a change to a socket of the client that was not welcomed yet (live() filter removed): the change overtakes the welcome.

mutations.name: ack-names-wrong-version
mutations.why: onSubmit acks an append with a version one past the one it appended.

mutations.name: confirm-reports-pending
mutations.why: confirm hands the adapter the in-flight ops plus pending as confirmed (engine.ts:516 with the wrong list): the client's confirmed document holds ops that are not in that change.
